title: Matched mirror bank (current-steering unit)
description: A bank of identical unit current sources, the building block of a current-steering DAC or a binary/thermometer bias array. One diode-connected unit device, the library's NMOS bias reference with its programmed current delivered by an ideal source, sets the reference; the bank is $N_{legs}$ copies of it, sized width-first as unit-device multiples (bank width = $N_{legs}$ times the unit) on the unit device's own $V_{GS}$, which is the gate wire every leg shares, so every element is a faithful replica and the full-scale current is $N_{legs}$ times the unit current, give or take the channel-length-modulation gain error between the reference diode point and the shared output rail. Matching is what limits a current-steering converter's linearity: each unit element has a Pelgrom current spread, and across $N_{legs}$ elements the worst-case accumulated error grows as the square root of $N$ (a random-walk bound), which is the estimate this sheet reports and budgets. Compliance is a single saturation voltage, since the bank shares one output rail; a cascoded bank (see the cascode mirror) would trade headroom for a flatter output. The unit reference is diode-connected, so its drop is read off the table rather than estimated. Every leg's gate is on the unit reference's diode node, so no gate is a port and nothing is solved; the shared output rail is held at $V_{out}$, and the supply the reference's ideal source draws from is a port.
